title: SCIM: Federated IdP sync grace window + audit-hold for safe deprovisioning
creator: Marco Liang
description:
Problem: When customers use federated SSO (SAML/OIDC) with connected IdPs, SCIM events for user deprovisioning can arrive in bursts or be followed by corrective admin actions at the IdP. Immediate deprovisioning on first SCIM DELETE leads to data loss, unexpected access churn, and noisy support/incident escalations. Existing retry logic handles transient API failures but does not capture the operational semantics of federated identities (sessions, active tokens, admin reversals).

Goal: Implement a protective 'audit-hold' mode for SCIM DELETE events originating from federated IdPs that defers final delete for a configurable grace window (default = 72h) while recording rich audit telemetry and offering fast manual release from the Console. During the hold period we should: 1) surface deprovision candidates in the Console with reason and source IdP; 2) keep a recoverable tombstone state that prevents resource reuse collisions; 3) run reconciliation checks (session/token activity, second SCIM events) to auto-abort hold when appropriate; 4) maintain end-to-end observability and SLA accounting.

Design proposal:
1) Event classification: augment incoming SCIM events with origin metadata (idp.type, idp.tenant_id, scim.event_id, delivered_at). Federated origin flag is set for configured enterprise IdPs.
2) Hold lifecycle: on federated DELETE -> convert user state to "audit_hold" (soft-deprovision) with metadata: hold_started_at, hold_expires_at, hold_reason, original_scim_payload. We will create a recoverable tombstone key (user_id:hold:<ts>) to block reclaims.
3) Reconciliation: background reconciler runs prioritized checks: 1) has active sessions/tokens (via session store), 2) second SCIM event within hold window (e.g., PATCH to re-enable), 3) admin unlatch via Console or API, 4) IdP-reported re-provision. If any check indicates user continues, we abort hold and mark as "reprovisioned" with audit link.
4) Auto-finalize/backoff: if hold_expires and no reconciling evidence, run final deprovision. On transient platform errors during finalize, employ exponential backoff with jitter (max 5 retries over 24h) and post to dead-letter for manual intervention after exhaust.
5) Console UX: new 'Held Deprovisions' view under Admin -> Users showing reason, hold age, last SCIM payload, attached audit entries, and Manual Release / Cancel actions. Manual Release triggers immediate finalization flow and logs operator id.
6) Audit logging: every state transition emits an audit event (hold_created, hold_aborted, hold_finalized, hold_manual_release) to the audit pipeline including operator, idp metadata, and linked SCIM event ids. Logs are retained according to enterprise retention config and exportable via CSV/Log sink.
7) Controls & config: tenant-level toggles: enable_audit_hold (bool), default_grace_window (integer hours), auto_reconcile_checks (list). System default = enabled for federated IdPs and disabled for local (managed) directories.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Pros: reduces accidental data loss from IdP mistakes, provides observable runway for manual validation, improves customer trust for federated setups.
- Cons: added complexity to deprovision lifecycle, potential to delay legitimate deprovisions (mitigated by manual release and short default window). We must be careful about retention/tombstone storage and ensure RBAC for Console release.

Metrics to add: held_deprovisions_total, held_deprovision_age_seconds (histogram), held_finalized_total, held_aborted_total, hold_manual_release_count, hold_reconcile_reasons (labels).

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for state transitions and retry/backoff paths.
- Integration tests simulating bursts of SCIM DELETE/PATCH and active session signals.
- Canary: enable for 5 pilot tenants (support+customer success identified) for 2 weeks with monitoring of held queue growth and manual release rate.
- Full: ramp to all federated customers after 4 weeks if stability and low false-positives.

Runbooks/Docs: add Runbook: "SCIM Held Deprovision Operations" and update SCIM integration docs for customer-facing expectations.

Open questions:
- Default window: 72h vs 48h? Discuss with CSMs (customer feedback indicates 72h preferred for enterprises).
- Disk/backing store for tombstones: use existing user-state store (Redis+DB) vs new compact tombstone table. Cost analysis pending.

Implementation owners: Priya (owner), Marco (server/runtime), Elena (console UX), Javier (telemetry).
comments: 2025-02-10 Marco Liang: Initial spike complete. Confirmed feasibility of adding hold flag in user-state without breaking existing reconcile flows. Prototype branch created: github.com/redwood/infra/compare/scim-audit-hold (WIP).

2025-02-14 Priya Shah: Design review with Security and Compliance. AGREE: must capture original SCIM payload and IdP signature headers for audit. Compliance: retention of audit events must be configurable per tenant. Added to design.
2025-02-20 Elena Morales: Mockups for Console 'Held Deprovisions' view in Figma: https://figma.com/file/ABC123/scim-held-deprovisions. Shared with PM for feedback.

2025-02-25 Marco Liang: Reconciler prototype integrated with session-store API. Found edge-case where long-lived refresh tokens can falsely indicate activity; adding check: last_token_refresh < 7d threshold configurable.

2025-03-01 QA: Integration tests passed for happy-path and abort-on-reprovision. Observed rare race (duplicate SCIM PATCH arrives during finalize) — adding idempotency guard using scim.event_id dedupe.
2025-03-03 Priya Shah: PR #8345 opened: github.com/redwood/identity/pull/8345. Requesting review from Marco, Elena, and Security. Canaries scheduled for 2025-03-10 for 5 tenants.
